reason: Section 75 is a large subdivision by-law content source with distinct topics for plan forms and layouts, public-purpose land and facilities, and approval/refusal details.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision by-law forms, layout standards, abutting access, and existing access contributions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 75(1) authorizes forms and fees, subdivision layout standards, lot access requirements, and conditions for upgrading or contributing to existing access.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the plan-form, layout, abutting-access, and existing-access contribution matters a subdivision by-law may contain.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land for public purposes, money in lieu, facilities, and subdivision agreements

evidenceText: land is to be set aside as land for public purposes

proposedGroups.reason: These provisions cover setting aside land, paying money in lieu, providing subdivision facilities, arranging security or deposits, crediting excess public-purpose land, and filing binding agreements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how subdivision by-laws may require public-purpose land, money in lieu, facilities, security, and binding subdivision agreements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision approval limits, street names, legal survey monuments, and tentative-plan fees

evidenceText: shall not approve a subdivision plan if

proposedGroups.reason: These provisions address refusal where land is unsuitable or prejudices future subdivision, street-name approval, survey monument standards, and type 1 or type 2 tentative-plan fees.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the subdivision by-law rules for unsuitable land, future subdivision prejudice, street names, legal survey monuments, and different tentative-plan fees.

reason: Section 76 is a coherent public-purpose land and special-account rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Public-purpose land sale and special account use

evidenceText: shall be set aside by the council as land for public purposes

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections govern setting aside land for public purposes, conditions for sale, and the special account for sale proceeds or money in lieu.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when public-purpose land may be sold and how money for public purposes must be held and spent.

reason: Section 77 is a large development-officer source with separate topics for exemptions and referrals, approval/refusal powers, special preconditions, and certification effects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development officer tentative-plan exemptions, submissions, referrals, and delegation

evidenceText: is the receiver of tentative and subdivision plan submissions

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(1) makes the development officer the receiver of plan submissions, authorizes several exemptions, requires forwarding of certain plans or easements, and allows delegation by eligible development officers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the development officer's submission, exemption, referral, and delegation powers in subdivision by-law administration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Tentative plan decisions and subdivision or instrument approval refusals

evidenceText: within six weeks of receiving an application

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(1) sets the six-week tentative plan approval or rejection duty, subdivision plan conformity approval, instrument examination, and mandatory or discretionary refusal grounds.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the development officer approves or rejects tentative plans, subdivision plans, and instruments for registration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assent, variance, and easement preconditions for subdivision plan approval

evidenceText: shall not be approved under paragraph (1)(k) unless

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(2) prevents approval of certain subdivision plans until streets or public-purpose land are assented to, variances are permitted in writing, and utility or other easements are resolved.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the extra preconditions for subdivision plans involving streets, public-purpose land, variances, or easements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Instrument certification, good-faith certification, and Director authority

evidenceText: shall be signified by a certificate endorsed on the instrument

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover approval of instruments outside subdivision by-laws, certificates accepted by the registrar, deemed proper good-faith certification, and Director authority in some local governments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how instrument approvals are certified and when certification is accepted, deemed proper, or handled by the Director.

reason: Section 78 separates subdivision variance powers for advisory bodies and development officers from notice and repeat-request limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Advisory committee or regional service commission subdivision variances

evidenceText: permit a reasonable variance from the requirements of a subdivision by-law

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 78(1) authorizes reasonable subdivision by-law variances, attached terms and conditions, and withdrawal of those terms by resolution on filing an approved amending plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an advisory committee or regional service commission may permit subdivision variances and control attached terms.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 78(2) gives the development officer variance powers for listed subdivision by-law requirements, with authority to require plan terms and withdraw them on filing an approved amending plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a development officer may permit subdivision variances and control attached terms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Neighbour notice and same-variance request limits

evidenceText: may give notice to owners of land in the neighborhood

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize notice to neighbouring owners and prevent the same variance request from being made to the other decision-maker after a determination.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the neighbour notice contents for subdivision variance requests and the limits on repeat variance requests.

reason: Section 79 contains distinct concepts for filed subdivision plans, added parcels, the prohibition on unfiled subdivision, and instrument information rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filed subdivision plan definition and parcels added to adjoining parcels
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections define a filed subdivision plan and state how parcels created to be added to adjoining parcels are treated depending on whether the conveyance occurred.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a filed subdivision plan is and how added-to-adjoining parcels are treated for subdivision and development.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision by filed plan only and rectification before instrument approval
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections prohibit subdivision by other means unless exempted and block instrument approval until a violation is rectified.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the filed-plan requirement for subdividing affected land and the consequence of violating it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision plan exceptions and instrument reference requirements
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections exempt building subdivision and certain remnant or deed transfers, require instruments to refer to plans, parcels, easements, or remnants, and preserve validity despite non-compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which transfers are outside section 79 and what information instruments should include for filed subdivision plans or remnants.

reason: Section 80 is a coherent list of subdivision exemptions with a refusal standard.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision exemptions for parcels, conveyances, easements, and refusal grounds

evidenceText: may exempt from a subdivision by-law

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections list the exemptions a development officer may grant and allow refusal when undesirable for development or inconsistent with the Act or by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which parcels or conveyances may be exempted from subdivision rules and when the development officer may refuse an exemption.

reason: Section 81 is a coherent tentative subdivision plan application and content rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Tentative subdivision plan application, required contents, review, and filing limits

evidenceText: shall submit to the development officer

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require an application and copies, list what the tentative plan must show, require a conformity review, and state approval is not shown on the plan and the tentative plan is not filed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a tentative subdivision plan application must include, how it is reviewed, and why it is not accepted for filing.

reason: Section 82 is a focused expiry rule for tentative plan approval or exemption.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: One-year expiry of tentative subdivision plan approval or exemption

evidenceText: null and void at the expiration of one year

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that approval or exemption becomes null and void after one year except for land covered by an approved corresponding subdivision plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when tentative subdivision plan approval or exemption expires and the limited exception for approved corresponding subdivision plans.

reason: Section 83 links approved or exempted tentative plans to laying out subdivision land and using legal survey monuments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Laying out streets, lots, blocks, public-purpose land, and survey monuments

evidenceText: may proceed in one or more stages to lay out the streets

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow staged layout according to the approved tentative plan or development officer instructions and require legal survey monuments meeting prescribed design and standards.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a person may lay out subdivision streets and parcels and what survey monument standard applies.
